steps.question: Which inbox rule triggered the alert, and who owns it?
steps.answer: ana.ruiz@contoso.com created rule '.' moving mail containing 'invoice;payment;bank;wire' to 'RSS Feeds' from 198.51.100.23

steps.question: Which of ana.ruiz@contoso.com's successful sign-ins don't match the user's baseline?
steps.answer: 3 sign-ins from 198.51.100.23, 198.51.100.41 (NL) with a headless-browser user agent; first at 13:21:15 UTC. MFA shows as satisfied by a token claim: consistent with adversary-in-the-middle session token theft, not password-only compromise.

steps.question: Did the attacker infrastructure sign in to any other account?
How did the attacker get in?
steps.answer: ana.ruiz@contoso.com clicked https://fabrikarn-sharepoint.com/s/q3-payment-schedule at 13:18:04 UTC (3 minutes before the first malicious sign-in), from an email sent by docs-share@fabrikam-invoices.com with subject 'Shared with you: Q3 vendor payment schedule'. The message had been placed in the Junk folder, so the user opened it from Junk.

steps.question: How wide was the phishing campaign, and who else interacted with it?
steps.answer: 19 recipients ({'Junked': 4, 'Delivered': 15}). Clicked through: ana.ruiz@contoso.com. Click blocked by Safe Links: kevin.ng@contoso.com.

steps.question: What persistence did the attacker establish?
steps.answer: 1 inbox rule(s) and 1 OAuth consent(s): app 'Mail Organizer Pro' granted Mail.ReadWrite Mail.Send offline_access User.Read. The OAuth grant survives a password reset and must be revoked separately.

steps.question: What did the attacker access?
steps.answer: 46 MailItemsAccessed events from attacker IPs via {'Mail Organizer Pro': 46} between 13:45 and 13:56 UTC.

steps.question: Did the attacker use the mailbox to commit fraud?
steps.answer: 3 emails with an external Reply-To (northwind.billing@outlook-mailbox.example) requesting changed bank details, sent to: marcus.green@contoso.com, billing@northwind-supplies.com, nina.rossi@contoso.com.

steps.question: Is the password spray seen earlier the same day part of this incident?
steps.answer: Unrelated: 203.0.113.200: 14 failures across 14 accounts, 0 successes. No successful sign-in, different infrastructure, and it ended 3.9 hours before the phishing email arrived.
